:::{#thm-epe-decomposition}
#### Bias, variance and noise

Suppose that, given $X_0 = x$,
the new outcome $Y_0$ has mean $\mean(x)$ and variance $\sigma^2$
and is independent of the training set $\trainset$,
and that $\E{g\paren{x; \trainset}^2} < \infty$.
Then the [expected squared prediction error at $x$](#def-epe)
is the squared [bias](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-prediction-bias)
of the prediction $g\paren{x; \trainset}$ as a prediction of $\mean(x)$,
plus its [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance),
plus $\sigma^2$:

$$
\epe{x} = \sqf{\E{g\paren{x; \trainset}} - \mean(x)}
+ \Var{g\paren{x; \trainset}} + \sigma^2.
$$ {#eq-epe-decomposition}

:::

::: proof
This is the [expected squared prediction error theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-prediction-error)
of the pds notes,
with $f(x_0) = \mean(x)$,
prediction $\hat f(x_0) = g\paren{x; \trainset}$,
and noise $\varepsilon = Y_0 - \mean(x)$,
applied conditionally on $X_0 = x$.
Given $X_0 = x$, that noise has mean 0 and variance $\sigma^2$,
and it is independent of $g\paren{x; \trainset}$
because $Y_0$ is independent of $\trainset$.
:::
